name: requirements-analysis
description: Analyses software user stories, extracts functional and non-functional requirements, evaluates acceptance criteria and identifies ambiguities. Use when analysing or improving software requirements from Jira or documents.

# Requirements Analysis

## 1. Understand the Source

- Read the complete user story and relevant context.
- Preserve the original meaning.
- Identify the business problem and expected outcome.
- Distinguish confirmed facts from assumptions.

## 2. Analyse Requirements

Identify:
- Functional requirements.
- Non-functional requirements.
- Business rules.
- User roles and permissions.
- Constraints and dependencies.
- External integrations.

## 3. Evaluate User Stories

Check whether each story clearly communicates:
- Who needs the functionality.
- What they need.
- Why they need it.
- Expected behaviour.
- Acceptance criteria.

Identify missing, ambiguous or conflicting information.

## 4. Acceptance Criteria

- Make criteria specific and testable.
- Cover successful and unsuccessful scenarios.
- Include relevant validation and boundary conditions.
- Avoid introducing unapproved behaviour.

## 5. Clarification

Ask focused questions when important information is missing.

Never invent answers or silently convert assumptions into requirements.

## 6. Jira Handling

- Preserve Jira issue keys and existing content.
- Separate original content from proposed improvements.
- Prepare proposed changes before publishing.
- Require explicit human approval before creating or updating issues.

## 7. Output Quality

Requirements must be:
- Clear
- Consistent
- Testable
- Traceable to their source
- Understandable to technical and non-technical stakeholders
